questions.corrige_markdown:
The statement $\sim p\vee q$ ("not $p$ or $q$") is true when at least one of $\sim p$ and $q$ is true, and false only when both are false.

| $p$ | $q$ | $\sim p$ | $\sim p\vee q$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | T |
| T | F | F | F |
| F | T | T | T |
| F | F | T | T |

Row by row: (F or T) = T; (F or F) = F; (T or T) = T; (T or F) = T.

**Last column: T, F, T, T.**
